title: Counterexample-Guided Reasoning Eval Pack (v1)
content:
- root_prompt: the canonical prompt text
- variant_tag: [canonical | paraphrase | unit_confusion | negation_case | formatting_trap]
- gold_answer: short canonical numeric or TRUE/FALSE string
- gold_steps: short bulletized canonical steps (only for onboarding annotations)
- difficulty: {easy,medium,hard} (string)
- failure_modes_expected: comma-separated short list (e.g., arithmetic-slip, unit-mix, hallucinated-step)

Scoring rubric (how we compute signals):
- Numeric correctness: exact-match on the canonical numeric value OR normalized-string-equality for algebraic answers. Scoring: 1 if exact, 0 if not.
- Step-consistency: if model outputs steps, use a lightweight checker: does the final numeric state's derivation match intermediate arithmetic? Score 1/0/NA (NA if CoT-suppressed).
- Verifier precision/recall: treat model TRUE/FALSE as binary classifier; compute precision/recall across verifier subset.
- Robustness delta (counterexample-sensitive): compute pass rate on canonical vs pass rate on corresponding counterexamples; if drop > 20 percentage points -> flag.

Baseline expectations (for onboarding):
- Internal baseline model "redwood-base-alpha": numeric correctness ~88% on seed-word-problems, step-consistency coverage 72% when allowed CoT, verifier precision 0.92 / recall 0.89.
- Release threshold for onboarding: any candidate model must meet numeric correctness >= 80% and not regress >5% absolute on any axis compared to last stable model.

Regression integration notes:
- CI job name: am-counterexample-smoke (runs nightly).
- Harness call: eval-harness run --suite counterexample-guided --seed 42 --mode quick --max-calls 500 (see linked GH PR for exact flags).
- Artifact outputs: CSV with columns id,prompt,model_output,score_numeric,score_steps,verifier_label,notes. Automatically uploaded to S3 path: s3://redwood-evals/counters/v1/{date}/results.csv (team infra will create bucket).

Examples (hand-curated failures we want to catch):
- Phrase-level trap: "If Alice has 2 more than half of Ben's marbles and together they have 26..." Many models mis-handle the "more than half" phrasing and produce arithmetic mistakes.
- Negation embedding: "Which of the following is NOT true: the combined age is 50; Alice is younger than Bob; Alice is 5 years older than Bob." Models often miss the NOT and select a true statement.
- Unit mixing: problems that swap counts and units to cause simple algebra to appear invalid if treated naively.

Data provenance and notes:
- Seeds come from public math-problem corpora (adapted and paraphrased) + hand-authored counterexamples. We keep provenance metadata in CONFLUENCE (linked above).
- Each prompt includes an internal canonical solution and a short verifier script (regex+small python grader) used by the harness.

Open issues / TODOs:
- Decide standard for tolerated textual variants of numeric answers (e.g., "twelve" vs "12"). Current harness normalizes digits but there are edge cases with fractions.
- Add a small module to detect when a model refuses to answer due to policy and mark those cases separately; right now refusals count as failures which skews ratios for safety-conscious models.
- Expand counterexample families to include adversarial tokenization traps (e.g., non-ASCII hyphens) — need infra support.

Quick checklist for onboarding run (for reviewer):
- [ ] Pull latest eval-harness (PR referenced above)
- [ ] Run local quick mode and inspect first 20 failures
- [ ] If any regression flagged, triage to developer and attach model prompt/response to JIRA-RED-4827
- [ ] For novel failure modes, add new counterexample variant to the seed file and tag owner

Contact and ownership:

- Contact: sofia.nguyen@redwood.ai (internal)

Change log (v1):

Notes-to-self: keep pack small and focused — we want high signal per-case. If we need broader coverage, create a separate "coverage" suite rather than bloat this counterexample smoke pack.
